title: Google began as a campus problem. Its first version, BackRub, used nearly half of Stanford's network
description:
Its first version, BackRub, used nearly half of Stanford's network bandwidth. It was released on the university website in August 1996.

Stanford PhD students who started the BackRub research project.

Andy Bechtolsheim wrote one for $100,000 in August 1998. It was made out to a corporation that did not yet exist.

Google was incorporated on 4 September 1998 in a friend's garage. The garage belonged to Susan Wojcicki in Menlo Park.

The company was funded before it was formed.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Google (read): established that Page and Brin started the BackRub research project at Stanford in 1996, that the first version was released in August 1996 and used nearly half of the university's network bandwidth, that google.com was registered on 15 September 1997, that Andy Bechtolsheim contributed $100,000 in August 1998 to a corporation that did not yet exist, and that Google was incorporated on 4 September 1998 in Susan Wojcicki's garage in Menlo Park.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Search (read): established that the Stanford phase of the search engine was nicknamed BackRub and that PageRank was developed in 1996 by Page, Brin and Scott Hassan.
